finalText:
It's a small Node app, five files, one request flow straight through.

```mermaid
flowchart LR
    A[server.js] -->|checks token| B[auth.js]
    A -->|handoff| C[routes.js]
    C -->|reads| D[cache.js]
    C -->|writes| E[store.js]
    D -->|cache miss| E
```

**server.js** — the front door. Plain Node HTTP server, checks the bearer token on every request, then passes it to the route table.

**auth.js** — turns a header like `Bearer <userId>.<sig>` into a user, by checking the signature against a shared secret.

**routes.js** — three endpoints: get a user, list orders, add an order. Reads go through the cache, writes go straight to the store.

**cache.js** — a small LRU, 256 entries, sits in front of the store for reads.

**store.js** — an in-memory stand-in for a real database. Each record expires 15 minutes after its last write.

One thing worth knowing: the cache has no expiry of its own. If a value gets cached, it can keep being served after the store's own copy has expired.
